finish_line_question_implication.question: Is the arrow shown once growth keeps making new sites one way while the written share holds steady, or must the number of written records keep rising?
finish_line_question_implication.growth_one_way: In every growing WW2 run Births far outnumber undos (1,735 Births to 7 undos in the no-bath headline; 218 to 2 with the heat bath), so new sites keep coming. That one-wayness is the counting arrow already on file (more ways forward than back), inside rate models, plus PD-29 wherever used-up carriers seed new growth points.
finish_line_question_implication.if_a_steady_written_share_is_enough: Without a bath the written share of new sites settles: about one half with the rules' pricing at the placeholder store value (0.50-0.55 at every size from 16 to 2,000 sites, with no added rule doing any work, but each record erased about once per write), and 0.62-0.69 with level absorption at the fast clock (0.17 at the 100-times-slower clock). With the heat bath and every move live, the share of new sites is 9-13% at doubling and 17-19% at four times the start, and the overall share is still falling by dilution: not shown steady. So under this reading WW2's no-bath runs would supply growth plus a settling share even without the added rule, but only in the rate models with links still and carriers sped up; the every-move test would not.
finish_line_question_implication.if_the_number_of_written_records_must_ke: Taken literally, the count of written records rises in every growing no-bath run and in the long heat-bath runs (432 -> 904-931), including the two-way readings where each record is erased about once per write: a rising count follows from growth plus a settling share (the seat's step 17). finish_line_question_implication.what_the_choice_turns_on: WW2 makes the split less about count versus share than about whether individual unbound records must stay written: under the share reading the native half-written equilibrium already qualifies in the rate model (PD-36 says only bound records must stay), while the stay-written reading needs PD-29, the matched store value and the hand-set clock.
